transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Heavy rain and flooding across parts of Alabama after Hurricane Isaias made landfall along
the Florida Panhandle last night as a Category 2 storm.
National Weather Service meteorologist Bob Oravec says the storm is weakened into a post-tropical
cyclone that continues to bring heavy rain to the region.
"It's still going to be producing some heavy rain today.
Heavy rain is going to be the main threat from this storm going forward.
The winds have calmed down a lot.
The flooding is still occurring along the coast, especially the storm surge flooding."
The storm is expected to move toward Tennessee, then northeast through the Appalachians.
Its remnants will bring rain and gusty winds to the mid-Atlantic this weekend.
In the Pacific, Hurricane Simon has strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm as it makes
its way toward the southwestern coast of Mexico.
The United States recently imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
The Trump administration says they're intended to block the court's access to U.S. technology
and financial services.
NPR's Emily Fang reports President Trump has also asked China to help him challenge
the court.
Starting after meeting with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing this past spring, President Trump
has repeatedly told the Chinese leader how much he dislikes the International Criminal
Court and has said the U.S. and China have a shared stance against the court, which Beijing
is not a member of, and which the Trump administration has said baselessly issued arrest warrants
for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a former Israeli Defense Minister.
Trump's raised these complaints about the ICC and possibilities for cooperation with
China on the matter with China's Xi several times this year.
That's according to three people familiar with these diplomatic discussions who are
not authorized to speak publicly.
Emily Fang and Pure News, Washington.
Delta Airlines says it's cutting its annual profit forecast amid surging jet fuel costs.
Marlon Hyde from member station WABE reports the company expects to pay an additional $6
billion for fuel this year.
Delta Airlines reported September quarter revenue of $17.6 billion up from the same
period last year.
That is all while spending more than 60% more on fuel.
Federal data shows airlines have raised ticket prices by more than 20% compared to last year
as companies have passed on rising fuel costs to customers.
However, Delta CEO Ed Bastian says the higher prices have largely not deterred travelers.
Resilient demand and greater focus on profitability are enabling the industry to recover higher
fuel costs more quickly.
Bastian expects demand to remain strong into next year when he hopes fuel will be cheaper.
For NPR News, I'm Marlon Hyde in Atlanta.
This is NPR News in Washington.
Two powerful earthquakes drug Panama Friday damaging buildings and prompting evacuations.
The U.S. Geological Survey says dozens of aftershocks have followed.
Injuries have been reported but authorities had not confirmed any deaths as of last night.
The Panama Canal remains opened with operations unaffected.
The tsunami warning that was issued after the quake struck has been lifted.
Security forces have shut down central New Delhi and detained protest leaders to prevent
demonstrations.
NPR's Diya Hadid reports the protests target a controversial revision of voter lists that
has removed millions of names.
Police boarded a flight that had just landed carrying protest leaders.
One leader, Abhijit Deepke, says in a video he shared online.
The police is here to arrest us.
Police also drag barricades across roads that lead to a protest site.
Police bled over a loudspeaker.
Police say they're preventing disorder.
The protests are over a controversial revision of voter rolls that has crossed millions of
people off electoral lists.
Critics allege the government is trying to disenfranchise voters who are unlikely to
vote for the ruling Hindu Nationalist Party led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The government has not responded to those accusations.
Diya Hadid, NPR News, New Delhi.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Heavy rain and flooding hit Alabama after Hurricane Isaias makes landfall on Florida Panhandle
Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 as it nears southwestern coast of Mexico
U.S. imposes new sanctions on International Criminal Court, blocking access to U.S. technology and finance
Trump reportedly asks China's Xi Jinping to help challenge the International Criminal Court
Delta Airlines cuts annual profit forecast as jet fuel costs surge, expects $6 billion extra fuel spending
Two powerful earthquakes strike Panama, damaging buildings; no deaths confirmed, canal operations unaffected
New Delhi police shut down central area and detain protest leaders over voter roll revision
Indian opposition protest leader Abhijit Deepke says police boarded his flight to arrest him
